advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the contract-reasoning scan enumerate contract-registering modules automatically (or assert the registry set matches an expected enumeration) rather than relying on a hardcoded import list that silently misses new modules.
evidence: tests/unit/test_output_contract_no_reasoning_in_output.py:38-45 hardcodes the module list: `for module in ("rebar.llm.code_review.contracts", "rebar.llm.plan_review.floors", "rebar.llm.plan_review.passes", "rebar.llm.plan_review.xcheck", "rebar.llm.review_kernel.verify_models")`
Docstring asserts: "The scan covers every registered contract, so a new contract cannot reintroduce the pattern."
search_files for `register_contract` shows an additional registrant not in the list: `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:321: register_contract(CONTRACT_NAME, _build_contract)`

Fail-open rationale: a newly-added contract module that is absent from this hardcoded import loop is never registered during the test, so `_descriptions` sees none of its fields — the test's PASS is indistinguishable from the scan never having examined the new contract.
advisory.finding: The new output-contract reasoning-scan test only imports a hardcoded list of contract-registering modules, so its docstring claim that "a new contract cannot reintroduce the pattern" fails open: a future offending contract in a module not added to this list is never imported, never scanned, and the parametrized test still passes green. The `len(names) >= 10` guard only proves SOME contracts loaded, not that every contract-registering module was imported.
scenarios: A developer adds a new review contract in a new module with an `analysis: Field(description='Scratchpad — reason first')` and forgets to add that module to this test's import loop — the production provider declines the request at runtime but the guard test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Discover contract modules by walking `rebar.llm` subpackages for a `register_contracts`/`register_contract` call (or pin the expected set of registered names explicitly and fail when `_CONTRACTS` contains an unexpected name), so an unlisted new contract fails the guard instead of being invisible.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge into any existing `bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields`/`output_config` rather than overwriting the key when setting effort.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:415-417: `model_settings["bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields"] = {"output_config": {"effort": caps.effort}}`
search_files shows `bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields` is set at only this one site today, so no current collision — but the assignment is a replace, not a merge.
The sibling comment notes native structured output is unmeasured for 5.5 (so no collision now), making this a latent rather than active bug.
advisory.finding: `build_model_settings` assigns `model_settings["bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields"]` to a fresh dict `{"output_config": {"effort": ...}}` unconditionally, overwriting the key wholesale. If any future code path (e.g. native structured output via `output_config.format` on Bedrock) also needs `additionalModelRequestFields`, this blind assignment would clobber it rather than merge.
scenarios: A later capability row enables Bedrock native json_schema output (which also rides additionalModelRequestFields) for a model that also pins effort — the effort assignment would drop the schema or vice-versa depending on ordering.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md built-in class defaults (lines ~473-474) to the 5.5 ids to match model_classes.py/config.py.
evidence: infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:473: "`_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS`): `frontier` = `claude-opus-4-8`, `standard` =`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `trivial` = `claude-haiku-4-5`."
monitoring_eb6e.tf:23 alarm_description: "Runbook: infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md, \"Kill-switch: revert the LLM path from Bedrock to direct Anthropic\""
config.py diff: DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-opus-5-5"; VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"; model_classes.py diff: TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"
advisory.finding: The kill-switch runbook cited by the Terraform alarm (monitoring_eb6e.tf line 23, "infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md, 'Kill-switch: revert the LLM path from Bedrock to direct Anthropic'") still documents the pre-5.5 built-in class defaults (claude-opus-4-8 / claude-sonnet-4-6 / claude-haiku-4-5). After this change the code defaults in model_classes.py and config.py are the 5.5 ids, so the runbook now misdescribes exactly which models the kill-switch restores — operational drift on the documented blast-radius mitigation.
scenarios: Operator executes the Bedrock→direct-Anthropic kill-switch during a Bedrock client-error incident and expects 4.x models per the runbook, but gets 5.5 (different temperature/effort request surface).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Refresh infra/runbooks/plan-review-eval-ops.md model ids (lines 44-47) to the 5.5 inference profiles consistent with the new ladder.
evidence: infra/runbooks/plan-review-eval-ops.md:45: "| Tier 2, full mode | 20 | `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | ..."
infra/runbooks/plan-review-eval-ops.md:44: "| Tier 1 | 60 | `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | ..."
rebar.toml diff moves frontier/standard/trivial classes to opus-5-5/sonnet-5-5/haiku-5-5
advisory.finding: The plan-review eval-ops runbook still pins the 4.x Bedrock inference profiles (claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-4-6) in its cost/usage table while the active ladder and provider overlays moved to 5.5, so the documented eval command ids no longer match the ids that are now invokable/metered.
scenarios: An operator copies the documented eval model id to reproduce a run and uses a now-superseded profile, producing cost/behavior that no longer reflects production.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/extend a test pinning the monitoring_eb6e.tf ModelId dimensions to the compose/overlay Bedrock ids so the two literal copies cannot drift undetected.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:95-96: "The cutover test pins these IDs to the CI provider matrix. Update the ModelId alarm in monitoring_eb6e.tf if any ID changes."
monitoring_eb6e.tf:42: "treat_missing_data = \"notBreaching\""
monitoring_eb6e.tf:80/91/102: dimensions = { ModelId = "us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5" } etc. are hand-maintained literals
ABSENCE: no test cited in the diff or rebar.toml ties the Terraform ModelId dimensions to the compose/overlay ids; the pin named (test_project_default_provider.py) covers overlay↔rebar.toml only
advisory.finding: The docker-compose comment at line 95-96 ('Update the ModelId alarm in monitoring_eb6e.tf if any ID changes') and the Terraform alarm encode the Bedrock ModelId dimensions as literal strings in two places that can only drift apart silently — there is no in-snapshot test visible that pins compose REBAR_LLM_*_MODEL to the Terraform ModelId dimensions (rebar.toml line 170 only mentions test_project_default_provider.py pinning overlay↔rebar.toml, not compose↔monitoring.tf). An alarm whose ModelId no longer matches the emitted metric silently stops dimensioning (treat_missing_data=notBreaching), so a client-error spike on the real model would never page.
scenarios: A future id change updates compose/overlays but misses monitoring_eb6e.tf (the comment is the only safeguard); the alarm then watches a nonexistent ModelId and, under notBreaching, never fires on a real 4xx spike.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether versioned/suffixed 5.5 inference-profile IDs exist and, if so, pin them for an immutable model revision (matching the prior 4.5 Haiku pinning posture); otherwise document that 5.5 profiles are intentionally unversioned.
evidence: Prior pinned id: `trivial  = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0" }`
New id: `trivial  = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5" }`
rebar.toml comment: "their suffixes are NOT uniform across generations — Haiku 4.5's carried `-20251001-v1:0`, the 5.5 profiles carry none (list-inference-profiles, us-east-1, 2026-11-09)"

The commit message asserts these are the inference profiles "listed in 896586841071/us-east-1 on 2026-11-09" but provenance rests on an out-of-band `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles` snapshot, not an immutable pinned revision.
advisory.finding: The new 5.5 Bedrock inference-profile IDs carry no version/date suffix, whereas the prior-generation Haiku ID was pinned with an immutable suffix (`-20251001-v1:0`). The unversioned aliases resolve to whatever the provider currently serves, so the pinned string no longer guarantees a fixed, reproducible model revision — a weaker provenance posture than the generation being replaced.
scenarios: AWS re-points the `claude-haiku-5-5` inference profile to a newer underlying model revision; rebar silently begins serving a different model with no diff and no lockstep failure.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/confirm a provenance artifact or verification that the six 5.5 inference-profile IDs match the provider's live list-inference-profiles output, not just internal two-sided agreement.
evidence: Comment: "Take any new id VERBATIM from that overlay (itself taken from `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region <region>`)."
Commit message: "The Bedrock ids are the inference profiles listed in 896586841071/us-east-1 on 2026-11-09"

ABSENCE: no changed file records the list-inference-profiles output or asserts the full set of six 5.5 IDs against a provenance fixture; two-sided pinning (test_project_default_provider.py) only checks rebar.toml<->bedrock.toml agreement, not provider-side existence.
advisory.finding: The provenance of the new model IDs rests entirely on an out-of-band claim (`aws bedrock list-inference-profiles` in account 896586841071/us-east-1 on 2026-11-09) recorded in the commit message and comments; there is no in-repo artifact (captured listing, checksum, or verification test asserting the exact id set) tying the pinned strings back to that snapshot.
scenarios: A typo'd or hallucinated 5.5 id is single-sourced consistently across all files, passes the two-sided pinning test, yet is not actually an invokable inference profile.
